messages:
sam: Heads-up — our traces for requests hitting /api/serve are missing root spans from collector-3 starting ~17:34 UTC. I can still see leaf spans in services, but nothing tying them to a root. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
maria: I saw similar gaps on the dashboard. Topology shows collector-3 restarted and its buffer cleared at the same time. Could be buffer reset evicting unflushed traces.
jon: +1. exporter queue spiked right before the restart. Logs show infinite retry loop against the OTLP endpoint for ~30s.
infra-oncall: Investigating. I pulled the collector logs: stack shows "failed to send: context deadline exceeded" and then a buffer truncate event. Attaching snippet.
tracing-bot: sample trace id: 0f5a3b2c — spans exist for svc-a and svc-b but no root span or traceparent in ingress. Excerpt: 
````
2026-03-18T17:33:58Z collector-3 exporter.go:142 error: send failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
2026-03-18T17:34:01Z collector-3 buffer.go:61 warn: dropped 1200 spans due to buffer reset
````
olga: This might be a propagation issue too — our edge proxy trims headers longer than 1024 bytes. If traceparent or baggage got long (we started adding route hints), proxy could be cutting the header and collector can't link.
sam: Good call. We recently added route hints to baggage in canary. Could be correlation of two failures: header truncated + exporter backlog -> reset.
maria: Repro steps proposed: send a request with long baggage (>1k) and then spike exporter latency to force buffer pressure. I can run from perf env.
jon: Quick mitigation: increase collector export timeout and buffer size, and temporarily disable adding route hints to baggage from canary. Suggest env changes: 
````
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_TIMEOUT=45s
COLLECTOR_BUFFER_MAX_SPANS=200000
````
infra-oncall: I'm rolling the timeout change now on collector-3, will monitor queue length. If spikes persist, rollback the baggage change in the canary.
deploy-bot: deploy started for collector-3 config change (job id: deploy-8823). ETA ~1m.
tracing-bot: Dashboards: trace retention spike on traces.ingress.queue and exporter.retry_count. Linked: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/trace-pipeline/pipeline-overview :hourglass_flowing_sand:
olga: If header trimming is causing orphan spans we should also add a short-term guard: drop route hints above 512 bytes before sending to proxy. That avoids traceparent corruption.
sam: Agreed. Maria — can you run the repro and attach raw headers so we can confirm trimming?
maria: Running now. If this reproduces I'll open INC-4321 and add reproduction steps + trace ids.
jon: Also let's add a retention fallback: when buffer flush fails, persist to local disk spool for 5m instead of immediate drop. That reduces lost-root scenarios.
infra-oncall: Noted — file an infra RFC for spool behavior. For incident, I'll keep collector-3 pinned to increased timeout and buffer. Will update in 10m.
sam: Thanks — timeline and next steps sound good. If we confirm header trimming + buffer pressure are the root cause, plan is: revert baggage change in canary, keep buffer/timeouts bumped, and implement spool + header guard in follow-up. :+1:
maria: Repro successful — attaching headers fragment in the incident ticket. Opening INC-4321 now.
tracing-bot: INC-4321 created by maria — https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-4321 — metadata: severity=P2, affected=collector-3, traces_lost~1200.
sam: Great work. Let's keep thread updates here. If anyone spots other collectors behaving the same ping @infra-oncall immediately.
